questions.text: Suppose you want to move from 0 to 100 on the number line. In each step, you either move right by a unit distance or you take a shortcut. A shortcut is simply a pre-specified pair of integers i,j with [latex]i \lt j[/latex]. Given a shortcut i, j if you are at position i on the number line, you may directly move to j. Suppose T(k) denotes the smallest number of steps needed to move from k to 100. suppose further that there is at most 1 shortcut involving any number, and in particular from 9 there is a shortcut to 15. Let y and z be such that T(9) = 1 + min(T(y), T(z)). Then the value of the product yz is_______.
questions.solution:
From 9 you can either step right to 10 or take the shortcut to 15.

[latex]T(9)=1+\min(T(10),T(15))[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] y, z = 10, 15

yz = 150

Answer: 150

questions.text: You have an array of n elements. Suppose you implement quick sort by always choosing the central element of the array as the pivot. Then the tightest upper bound for the worst case performance is
questions.solution:
Choosing the middle element is still a fixed rule. An adversary can arrange the input so the middle element is always the smallest or largest, giving partitions of size n[latex]-[/latex]1 and 0 every time.

[latex]T(n)=T(n-1)+O(n)=O(n^2)[/latex]

Answer: [latex]O(n^2)[/latex]

questions.text: Suppose depth first search is executed on the graph below starting at some unknown vertex. Assume that a recursive call to visit a vertex is made only after first checking that the vertex has not been visited earlier. Then the maximum possible recursion depth (including the initial call) is _________.
questions.solution:
Max recursion depth = number of vertices on the longest simple path DFS can follow.

- Left 3 [latex]\times[/latex] 3 grid: a snake path covers all 9 vertices, ending at its bottom-right corner.
- Bottom middle vertex: 1 (its pendant above is a dead end, so skip it).
- Right 3 [latex]\times[/latex] 3 grid: enter at the bottom-left corner; we must end at the middle-right vertex to reach the pendant. A grid is bipartite (5 corner-coloured, 4 other), so a corner-to-middle path can cover only 8 vertices.
- Right pendant: 1

Depth = 9 + 1 + 8 + 1 = 19

Answer: 19

questions.text: The number of distinct minimum spanning trees for the weighted graph below is
questions.solution:
Use Kruskal. All weight-1 edges are taken (they form no cycle), leaving components: {top-left, centre, left, bottom}, {top-right, right}, {triangle edge pair of weight 1}, {triangle's bottom-left vertex}.

Now weight-2 edges:
- Join the two left components: 3 choices (top edge, centre-top-right, centre-right).
- The long bottom edge is the only link to the triangle [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] forced.
- Join the triangle's last vertex: 2 choices (either weight-2 edge of the triangle).

Number of MSTs = 3 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 = 6

Answer: 6

questions.text:
Suppose P, Q, R, S, T are sorted sequences having lengths 20, 24, 30, 35, 50 respectively.
They are to be merged into a single sequence by merging together two sequences at a time.
The number of comparisons that will be needed in the worst case by the optimal algorithm for doing this is ____.
questions.solution:
Merging lists of size m and n needs m + n [latex]-[/latex] 1 comparisons in the worst case. Optimal: always merge the two smallest (like Huffman).

- 20 + 24 = 44 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 43
- 30 + 35 = 65 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 64
- 44 + 50 = 94 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 93
- 65 + 94 = 159 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 158

Total = 43 + 64 + 93 + 158 = 358

Answer: 358
